"""
    expand_flux_guided!(sp, model, rates, t, bc, flux_tolerance) -> (Φ_total, λ_max)

Unified flux-guided expansion.  For each active state x with p(x) > 0 and each
reaction k, the neighbor x+νk is added to the active set when the per-reaction
outflux α_k(x)·p(x) exceeds `flux_tolerance · Φ_total`.

Returns `(Φ_total, λ_max)` where
  Φ_total = Σᵢ p(xᵢ)·w(xᵢ)  (probability-weighted total exit rate, pre-expansion)
  λ_max   = maxᵢ w(xᵢ)       (maximum total exit rate, including newly added states)

`λ_max` covers newly added states (p=0 at time t) because the max-propensity cap
uses it to bound the time step: newly added states will receive probability during
the step, and their fast rates must be accounted for.
"""
function expand_flux_guided!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc,
                              flux_tolerance::Real) where {E,T}
    n_orig = length(sp)
    n_rxn  = length(model.stoichvecs)

    # Pass 1: compute per-reaction propensities for original states;
    #         accumulate Φ_total and λ_max over original states.
    props   = Matrix{Float64}(undef, n_orig, n_rxn)
    Φ_total = 0.0
    λ_max   = 0.0
    @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
        x = sp.states[i]
        w = 0.0
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            α = max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
            props[i, k] = α
            w += α
        end
        Φ_total += sp.probs[i] * w
        λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
    end

    # Pass 2: flux-guided expansion (reuse saved propensities for efficiency).
    flux_threshold = Φ_total * flux_tolerance
    @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
        p_x = sp.probs[i]
        p_x <= 0.0 && continue
        x = sp.states[i]
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            props[i, k] * p_x > flux_threshold || continue
            y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
            haskey(sp.index, y) && continue
            bc(y) || continue
            add_state!(sp, y)
        end
    end

    # Pass 3: extend λ_max to cover newly added states (p=0, but fast rates
    #         matter for the max-propensity cap on the time step).
    @inbounds for i in (n_orig + 1):length(sp)
        x = sp.states[i]
        w = 0.0
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            w += max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
        end
        λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
    end

    (Φ_total, λ_max)
end

"""
    expand_adaptive!(sp, model, rates, t, bc, ε_dt, flux_tolerance) -> (Φ_total, λ_max)

Unified adaptive expansion governed by the spatial stiffness ratio
κ = λ_max / Φ_total:

- **Low-stiffness** (κ·ε_dt ≤ 1): for each active state x, add the
  highest-propensity neighbor not already in J.  This is the deterministic
  analog of SSA expansion — adds one directional neighbor per state and avoids
  exponential state-space inflation in oscillatory systems.

- **High-stiffness** (κ·ε_dt > 1): flux-guided expansion — add neighbor x+νk
  whenever α_k(x)·p(x) > flux_tolerance·Φ_total.  The max-propensity cap
  (1/λ_max) limits the time step in this regime, so only dominant flux
  directions need covering.

Returns `(Φ_total, λ_max)` where
  Φ_total = Σᵢ p(xᵢ)·w(xᵢ)  (pre-expansion; unchanged by adding p=0 states)
  λ_max   = maxᵢ w(xᵢ)       (post-expansion; includes newly added states for cap)
"""
function expand_adaptive!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc,
                           ε_dt::Real, flux_tolerance::Real) where {E,T}
    n_orig = length(sp)
    n_rxn  = length(model.stoichvecs)

    # Pass 1: compute propensities once for all original states;
    #         accumulate Φ_total and λ_max.
    props   = Matrix{Float64}(undef, n_orig, n_rxn)
    Φ_total = 0.0
    λ_max   = 0.0
    @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
        x = sp.states[i]
        w = 0.0
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            α = max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
            props[i, k] = α
            w += α
        end
        Φ_total += sp.probs[i] * w
        λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
    end

    κ = Φ_total > 0.0 ? λ_max / Φ_total : 1.0

    # Pass 2: expand according to stiffness regime.
    if κ * ε_dt <= 1.0
        # Low-stiffness: greedy expansion — add the highest-propensity neighbor
        # not already in J (deterministic SSA analog, one new state per active state).
        @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
            k_best = 0; α_best = 0.0
            x = sp.states[i]
            for k in 1:n_rxn
                props[i, k] <= α_best && continue
                y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
                haskey(sp.index, y) && continue
                bc(y) || continue
                α_best = props[i, k]
                k_best = k
            end
            k_best == 0 && continue
            add_state!(sp, x + model.stoichvecs[k_best])
        end
    else
        # High-stiffness: flux-guided expansion — add directions where α·p exceeds
        # threshold.  Cap (1/λ_max) handles the time step; expansion need only cover
        # states that will receive non-negligible probability during the step.
        flux_threshold = Φ_total * flux_tolerance
        @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
            p_x = sp.probs[i]
            p_x <= 0.0 && continue
            x = sp.states[i]
            for k in 1:n_rxn
                props[i, k] * p_x > flux_threshold || continue
                y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
                haskey(sp.index, y) && continue
                bc(y) || continue
                add_state!(sp, y)
            end
        end
    end

    # Pass 3: extend λ_max to newly added states (p=0 but fast rates cap the step).
    @inbounds for i in (n_orig + 1):length(sp)
        x = sp.states[i]
        w = 0.0
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            w += max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
        end
        λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
    end

    (Φ_total, λ_max)
end

"""
    StateSpace{E, T<:Real}

Tracks active states, their probabilities, and a stable global ID mapping.

- `states[i]` is the i-th active state.
- `probs[i]`  is its probability.
- `index[x]`  gives the compact position of state `x` in `states`.
- `global_id[x]` gives the permanent ID assigned when `x` was first added.
- `id_to_state[id]` maps permanent ID back to state (append-only).
- `next_id` is the next global ID to assign.
"""
mutable struct StateSpace{E, T<:Real}
    states::Vector{E}
    probs::Vector{T}
    index::Dict{E,Int}
    global_id::Dict{E,Int}
    id_to_state::Vector{E}
    next_id::Int
end

function StateSpace{E,T}() where {E,T<:Real}
    StateSpace{E,T}(E[], T[], Dict{E,Int}(), Dict{E,Int}(), E[], 1)
end

Base.length(sp::StateSpace) = length(sp.states)

"""
    add_state!(space, state, prob=0.0)

Add `state` with probability `prob`. No-op if already present. O(1).
"""
function add_state!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, state::E, prob::T=zero(T)) where {E,T}
    haskey(sp.index, state) && return sp
    push!(sp.states, state)
    push!(sp.probs, prob)
    sp.index[state] = length(sp.states)
    if !haskey(sp.global_id, state)
        sp.global_id[state] = sp.next_id
        push!(sp.id_to_state, state)
        sp.next_id += 1
    end
    sp
end

"""
    remove_states!(space, mask)

Remove states where `mask[i] == true`. Rebuild compact index.
"""
function remove_states!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, remove_mask::BitVector) where {E,T}
    keep = .!remove_mask
    sp.states = sp.states[keep]
    sp.probs = sp.probs[keep]
    empty!(sp.index)
    for (i, s) in enumerate(sp.states)
        sp.index[s] = i
    end
    sp
end

"""
    expand!(space, model, bc; depth=1)

Add stoichiometric neighbors of all current states that satisfy `bc`.
Probabilities of new states are initialized to zero.
"""
function expand!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    for _ in 1:depth
        current = copy(sp.states)
        for x in current
            for ν in model.stoichvecs
                y = x + ν
                if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
                    add_state!(sp, y)
                end
            end
        end
    end
    sp
end

"""
    expand_flux_guided!(sp, model, rates, t, bc, flux_tolerance) -> (Φ_total, λ_max)

Unified flux-guided expansion.  For each active state x with p(x) > 0 and each
reaction k, the neighbor x+νk is added to the active set when the per-reaction
outflux α_k(x)·p(x) exceeds `flux_tolerance · Φ_total`.

Returns `(Φ_total, λ_max)` where
  Φ_total = Σᵢ p(xᵢ)·w(xᵢ)  (probability-weighted total exit rate, pre-expansion)
  λ_max   = maxᵢ w(xᵢ)       (maximum total exit rate, including newly added states)

`λ_max` covers newly added states (p=0 at time t) because the max-propensity cap
uses it to bound the time step: newly added states will receive probability during
the step, and their fast rates must be accounted for.
"""
function expand_flux_guided!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc,
                              flux_tolerance::Real) where {E,T}
    n_orig = length(sp)
    n_rxn  = length(model.stoichvecs)

    # Pass 1: compute per-reaction propensities for original states;
    #         accumulate Φ_total and λ_max over original states.
    props   = Matrix{Float64}(undef, n_orig, n_rxn)
    Φ_total = 0.0
    λ_max   = 0.0
    @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
        x = sp.states[i]
        w = 0.0
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            α = max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
            props[i, k] = α
            w += α
        end
        Φ_total += sp.probs[i] * w
        λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
    end

    # Pass 2: flux-guided expansion (reuse saved propensities for efficiency).
    flux_threshold = Φ_total * flux_tolerance
    @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
        p_x = sp.probs[i]
        p_x <= 0.0 && continue
        x = sp.states[i]
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            props[i, k] * p_x > flux_threshold || continue
            y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
            haskey(sp.index, y) && continue
            bc(y) || continue
            add_state!(sp, y)
        end
    end

    # Pass 3: extend λ_max to cover newly added states (p=0, but fast rates
    #         matter for the max-propensity cap on the time step).
    @inbounds for i in (n_orig + 1):length(sp)
        x = sp.states[i]
        w = 0.0
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            w += max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
        end
        λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
    end

    (Φ_total, λ_max)
end

"""
    expand_ssa!(space, model, rates, t, bc; depth=1)

Legacy SSA-style expansion: for each active state, sample one reaction by
propensity and add the sampled successor if it satisfies `bc`.
"""
function expand_ssa!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc; depth::Int=1) where {E,T}
    n_rxn = length(model.stoichvecs)
    n_rxn == 0 && return sp

    for _ in 1:depth
        current = copy(sp.states)
        for x in current
            props = Vector{Float64}(undef, n_rxn)
            total = 0.0
            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
                α = Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t))
                α = max(0.0, α)
                props[k] = α
                total += α
            end
            total <= 0 && continue

            threshold = rand() * total
            csum = 0.0
            chosen = 0
            @inbounds for k in 1:n_rxn
                csum += props[k]
                if threshold <= csum
                    chosen = k
                    break
                end
            end
            chosen == 0 && continue

            y = x + model.stoichvecs[chosen]
            if !haskey(sp.index, y) && bc(y)
                add_state!(sp, y)
            end
        end
    end
    sp
end

"""
    compress!(space, model, rates, t, prob_quantile; flux_tolerance=1e-6)

Flux-aware pruning with legacy count-quantile candidate selection.

Candidates are chosen by state count:
`round(prob_quantile * n_states)` lowest-probability states.
If `flux_tolerance <= 0`, all candidates are pruned.
Returns `(total_flux, n_removed)`.
"""
function compress!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real,
                   prob_quantile::Real; flux_tolerance::Real=1e-6) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return (zero(T), 0)

    # Compute flux for each state: p(x) * sum_k a_k(x)
    flux = Vector{T}(undef, n)
    @inbounds for i in 1:n
        w = zero(T)
        for prop in model.propensities
            w += prop(sp.states[i], rates, t)
        end
        flux[i] = sp.probs[i] * w
    end
    total_flux = sum(flux)
    flux_threshold = total_flux * flux_tolerance

    idx = sortperm(sp.probs)
    n_remove = round(Int, clamp(prob_quantile, 0, 1) * n)
    candidates = n_remove > 0 ? idx[1:min(n_remove, n)] : Int[]

    remove_mask = falses(n)
    n_removed = 0
    if flux_tolerance <= 0
        for i in candidates
            remove_mask[i] = true
            n_removed += 1
        end
    else
        for i in candidates
            if flux[i] < flux_threshold
                remove_mask[i] = true
                n_removed += 1
            end
        end
    end

    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
    (total_flux, n_removed)
end

"""
    prune_threshold!(space, threshold; max_probs=nothing)

Simple threshold-based pruning: remove states whose probability (or lookback-window
max probability, if `max_probs` is provided) is below `threshold`.
Returns the number of states removed.
"""
function prune_threshold!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, threshold::Real;
                          max_probs::Union{Nothing, Dict{E,<:Real}}=nothing) where {E,T}
    n = length(sp)
    n == 0 && return 0
    remove_mask = falses(n)
    n_removed = 0
    for i in 1:n
        p = max_probs !== nothing ? get(max_probs, sp.states[i], sp.probs[i]) : sp.probs[i]
        if p < threshold
            remove_mask[i] = true
            n_removed += 1
        end
    end
    remove_states!(sp, remove_mask)
    n_removed
end

"""
    renormalize!(space)

Scale probabilities so they sum to 1. Returns the sum before normalization.
"""
function renormalize!(sp::StateSpace)
    s = sum(sp.probs)
    if s > 0
        sp.probs ./= s
    end
    s
end

"""
    get_global_ids(space) -> Vector{Int}

Return the global IDs of the current active states (in compact order).
"""
function get_global_ids(sp::StateSpace)
    [sp.global_id[s] for s in sp.states]
end

<analysis>
Let me carefully analyze this conversation from start to finish.

## Session Start Context
This is a continuation from a previous session. The MEMORY.md shows the project is DiscStochSim.jl, a Julia package implementing adaptive FSP for stochastic chemical kinetics. The previous session had done significant work on:
- Adding flux_method and expand_method parameters to AdaptiveFSP
- Implementing corrected KrylovFSP
- Updating paper sections

## This Session's Work

### 1. Paper Theory Section Updates (Main task at session start)
The user confirmed 4 items to add to the paper:
1. Redo cor:flux-timestep connecting Φ_total and Φ_max to κ (spatial stiffness)
2. Connect SSA/stoich expansion to cor:expansion-depth
3. Add remark formally justifying max-propensity cap
4. Formalize Φ_max case

The assistant read paper/ex_article.tex lines 570-787 to understand the existing theory sections, then made three edits:

**Edit 1**: Replaced cor:flux-timestep (lines 682-709) with new unified version presenting two rules:
- Total-flux rule: Δt = ε_Δt/Φ_total, exact error ≤ ε_Δt, μ = κ·ε_Δt
- Maximum-flux rule: Δt = ε_Δt/Φ_max, error ≤ η·ε_Δt, μ = (λ_max/Φ_max)·ε_Δt
With unified proof establishing ||ε||₁ ≲ Φ_total·Δt as key bound, then applying each rule.

Added new rem:max-propensity-cap: cap Δt = min(ε_Δt/Φ_total, 1/λ_max) ensures μ ≤ 1 always.

**Edit 2**: Added rem:expansion-strategy after cor:expansion-depth proof:
- Stoich expansion: conservative, all R channels, appropriate κ>1
- SSA expansion: efficient, dominant channel, appropriate κ≈1

**Edit 3**: Updated rem:consistent-params to include all three time-step options, SSA/stoich selection, and updated bottleneck example.

**Error fixed**: enumerate[(i)] required the `enumerate` LaTeX package which wasn't loaded. Fixed by adding `\usepackage{enumerate}` to preamble. Document compiled cleanly.

Also fixed reference range `Remarks~\ref{rem:max-propensity-cap}--\ref{rem:expansion-strategy}` to use individual references to avoid incorrect range spanning corollaries.

### 2. Discussion: Unified Framework
User raised concern: "I feel like the framework is still not fully adaptive; and is a little fragmented. I think if we adaptively expand we don't need expand_ssa. discuss to have one fundamental smooth unifying method for expansion, time stepping and pruning"

The assistant provided detailed analysis showing:
- Expansion and pruning are dual operations with the same flux criterion
- Flux-guided expansion: add x+νk if α_k(x)·p(x) > ε_flux·Φ_total
- Cap subsumes all flux_method choices
- SSA is deterministic flux-guided (dominant direction per state)

### 3. User's Response to Discussion
User confirmed the plan with specific points:
1. "I think the cap shouldn't be a problem. If there is a large time step there has to be a large expansion depth"
2. "yes sounds about right" (flux-guided)
3. "yes, lets revisit this based on the results" (missing directions concern)

    ```julia
    function expand_adaptive!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc,
                               ε_dt::Real, flux_tolerance::Real) where {E,T}
        n_orig = length(sp)
        n_rxn  = length(model.stoichvecs)

        # Pass 1: compute propensities, Φ_total, λ_max for original states
        props   = Matrix{Float64}(undef, n_orig, n_rxn)
        Φ_total = 0.0; λ_max = 0.0
        @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
            x = sp.states[i]; w = 0.0
            for k in 1:n_rxn
                α = max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
                props[i, k] = α; w += α
            end
            Φ_total += sp.probs[i] * w; λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
        end

        κ = Φ_total > 0.0 ? λ_max / Φ_total : 1.0

        if κ * ε_dt <= 1.0
            # Low-stiffness: greedy (argmax propensity per state, deterministic SSA)
            @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
                k_best = 0; α_best = 0.0; x = sp.states[i]
                for k in 1:n_rxn
                    props[i, k] <= α_best && continue
                    y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
                    haskey(sp.index, y) && continue; bc(y) || continue
                    α_best = props[i, k]; k_best = k
                end
                k_best == 0 && continue
                add_state!(sp, x + model.stoichvecs[k_best])
            end
        else
            # High-stiffness: flux-guided (α·p > threshold)
            flux_threshold = Φ_total * flux_tolerance
            @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
                p_x = sp.probs[i]; p_x <= 0.0 && continue
                x = sp.states[i]
                for k in 1:n_rxn
                    props[i, k] * p_x > flux_threshold || continue
                    y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
                    haskey(sp.index, y) && continue; bc(y) || continue
                    add_state!(sp, y)
                end
            end
        end

        # Pass 3: λ_max for newly added states (p=0 but cap needs their rates)
        @inbounds for i in (n_orig + 1):length(sp)
            x = sp.states[i]; w = 0.0
            for k in 1:n_rxn
                w += max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
            end
            λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
        end

        (Φ_total, λ_max)
    end
    ```
